original_question: Given a function kappa in C^-1(0,+infinity), what conditions are necessary and sufficient for kappa to belong to the class Ln of generalized Sonine-kernel pairs satisfying (kappa * k)(t) = 1^{<n>}(t), and how can one derive a representation of the associated kernel k?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, open problem 7: “For a function κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞), determine the conditions for the inclusion κ ∈ ℒ_n and derive a representation for the associated kernel k.” The precise surrounding setup is given in Section 2.3, especially Definition 2 and Theorem 7. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target unusually well: it uses the correct ambient class for κ, names the intended class ℒ_n, includes the defining generalized Sonine-type convolution identity, and asks for exactly the two things the paper asks for in open problem 7—membership criteria and a representation of the associated kernel k. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
missing_details: You need to fix the parameter n ∈ ℕ explicitly; ℒ_n depends on this chosen positive integer, and the problem is not well-posed without it. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

ℒ_n is a class of pairs (κ,k), not of κ alone. So a fully stand-alone formulation must ask for conditions on κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞) guaranteeing the existence of some k with (κ,k) ∈ ℒ_n. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The second kernel must satisfy the hidden regularity assumption k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞), not merely the convolution identity. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The function class notation must be defined: C_{α,β}(0,+∞) = {f : f(t)=t^p f_1(t), t>0, α<p<β, f_1 ∈ C[0,+∞)}, so in particular C_{-1}(0,+∞)=C_{-1,+∞}(0,+∞). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
The convolution is the Laplace convolution on the positive semi-axis, so the identity is required for all t>0. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9))

The notation 1^{<n>} must be unpacked: f^{<n>}=f*⋯*f (n-fold convolution), and {1}^{<n>}(t)=h_n(t)=t^{n−1}/(n−1)!. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The phrase “associated kernel k” should be tied to Definition 2: it means a kernel k for which (κ*k)(t)=1^{<n>}(t) and the stated class inclusions hold; the paper does not assert uniqueness here. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

Nearby context from Theorem 7 should be acknowledged because it is the closest explicit construction in the paper: if (κ,k) ∈ ℒ_1, then κ_n=( {1}^{<n−1>} * κ ) and k_n=k define a pair in ℒ_n. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

If you want the question to be fully paper-faithful, it helps to note that the n=1 case is separated in the preceding open problem 6; your draft is specifically the ℒ_n version, i.e. open problem 7. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
refined_question: For a fixed integer n ∈ ℕ, characterize all kernels κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞)=C_{-1,+∞}(0,+∞) for which there exists a kernel k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) such that, with Laplace convolution on (0,+∞), (κ*k)(t)={1}^{<n>}(t)=h_n(t)=t^{n−1}/(n−1)! for every t>0; equivalently, determine when there exists a pair (κ,k) ∈ ℒ_n in the sense of Definition 2, and derive a representation formula for the associated kernel k. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for fixed n ∈ ℕ, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞) for the existence of k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) such that (κ,k) belongs to ℒ_n, where by definition this means exactly that (κ*k)(t)={1}^{<n>}(t) for all t>0. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting open problem 7, not the neighboring finite-interval problems and not open problem 6, because it explicitly mentions κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞), the class ℒ_n, and the generalized Sonine identity with {1}^{<n>}. The exact hidden assumptions needed to make that question stand-alone come from Definition 2 in Section 2.3, while Theorem 7 is the closest nearby result because it gives the main explicit construction of kernels in ℒ_n from a Sonine pair in ℒ_1. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
